findings.title: Equal `order()` values make provider selection depend on classpath order
findings.description:
`detectProvider` sorts by `order()` and takes the first entry. Default, FIPS and Elytron all return 200 (`crypto/default/.../DefaultCryptoProvider.java:84`, `crypto/fips1402/.../FIPS1402Provider.java:115`, `crypto/elytron/.../WildFlyElytronProvider.java:77`). `sorted` is stable, so a tie is resolved by `ServiceLoader` discovery order, which follows the classpath. The old code threw "Multiple crypto providers loaded"; the new code silently picks one.

This matters for `integration/client-cli/client-cli-dist/assembly.xml:58-65`. That assembly copies both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` into `bin/client/lib`. `Globals.main` (`integration/client-cli/admin-cli/src/main/java/org/keycloak/client/cli/common/Globals.java:44`) auto-detects over that directory, so the CLI can run with either provider. In a FIPS setup that could mean non-FIPS crypto. The Quarkus server path calls `CryptoIntegration.setProvider` explicitly (`quarkus/runtime/.../KeycloakRecorder.java:214`), so the tie mainly affects auto-detect paths.

Also, line 69 passes a non-literal string to `logger.debugf`, and the message ends with a stray ", ".

Suggested fix: give FIPS a strictly higher order than default, or throw when the top two orders are equal so the ambiguity stays loud.

findings.title: DER decoder breaks its `IOException` contract on malformed input
findings.description:
Today the only input is DER produced by the local JDK: `ECDSAAlgorithm.asn1derToConcatenatedRS` (`core/.../ECDSAAlgorithm.java:49-50`), called from `ECDSASignatureSignerContext`. So this is latent, not exploitable now. But `ECDSACryptoProvider` is public, and the method is declared to throw `IOException` on bad input. The decoder does not do that:

- `readLength` returns -1 for indefinite length (lines 133-135). `readInteger` passes that to `read(length)` (line 72), which runs `new byte[-1]` (line 170) and throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException`.
- A zero-length INTEGER reaches `new BigInteger(bytes)` (line 73) with an empty array, which throws an unchecked `NumberFormatException`.
- `readNext` (lines 80-82) computes `length += reset()`. For an indefinite-length element that gives `-1 + headerBytes`, a wrong element size, instead of an error.
- `readSequence` (lines 55-61) subtracts element sizes from the content length without checking that elements stay inside the sequence, and ignores trailing bytes.
- On the conversion side, `integerToBytes` (`AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151-163`) silently truncates values wider than the coordinate size instead of rejecting them.

Suggested fix: reject 0x80 lengths and zero-length integers with `IOException`, check element bounds against the sequence length, and reject r or s that is negative or wider than `len`.

findings.title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns a JDK KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.description:
The interface documents this method as returning the BouncyCastle provider (`common/.../CryptoProvider.java:34-37`). This implementation returns the provider of `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType())`, which is a JDK provider (typically SUN for PKCS12).

`BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` (`common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/BouncyIntegration.java:31-40`) is a `static final` value computed once from this method. If this stub wins detection, the wrong provider name is fixed for the life of the JVM. The method also creates a new KeyStore on every call.

Suggested fix: return `null`, which `BouncyIntegration` already handles (lines 35-37), or return the provider this module actually relies on.

findings.title: New abstract `order()` on the public SPI breaks external implementers
findings.description:
All four implementations in this repo now define `order()`, so the tree is consistent. Out-of-tree `CryptoProvider` implementations will fail to compile, and an older jar will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError`.

Suggested fix: declare `default int order()` with a documented lowest-priority value so external providers keep working.

findings.title: ECDSA tests check only internal round-trip and do not cover the new behavior
findings.description:
- The only assertion (line 56) is that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rs))` equals `rs`. The JDK-produced DER (line 52) and the re-encoded DER (line 54) are never checked with `Signature.verify`. A conversion error that is symmetric in both directions still passes.
- Keys are not matched to curves. `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (line 42) uses default parameters, so the ES256/384/512 tests (lines 59-71) do not exercise their real curves or coordinate sizes.
- There are no negative tests for the decoder or encoder, which is where the previous finding lives: malformed DER, indefinite length, zero-length INTEGER, wrong sequence size.
- Nothing tests the new `order()`-based selection in `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider`, including the tie case.

Suggested fix: generate keys per curve (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1), verify the converted signature with `Signature.verify`, and add malformed-input cases that assert `IOException`.

findings.title: Two unused statements in the DER encoder
findings.description: Lines 114-115 create two `ASN1Encoder` instances, call `write` on them, and discard the results. They have no effect and the return statement below already encodes the same values. Remove them.

findings.title: Hamcrest is declared but never used
findings.description: The only test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:27-28`) imports `org.junit.Assert` and `org.junit.Test`. Nothing in `authz/client` uses Hamcrest. Drop it unless planned tests need it. The JUnit dependency itself is managed in the root POM (`junit.version`, root `pom.xml:565`).

findings.title: `AuthzClient.create` mutates JVM-global crypto state
findings.description: `CryptoIntegration.init` is JVM-wide and first-wins (`CryptoIntegration.java:29-38`). All three `create` overloads reach this line (lines 60-63, 72-82), so it always runs. If the first caller's classloader sees only this module's stub, that stub is locked in for the whole JVM. The POM describes this artifact as testsuite-only (`authz/client/pom.xml:18-19`), which lowers the risk. If it stays, document the side effect in the Javadoc.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace-only edits widen the diff
findings.description: Trailing spaces are removed in `CryptoProvider.java`, `DefaultCryptoProvider.java` and `FIPS1402Provider.java`, none of which relate to the change. Consider reverting them in this PR.
